h1: Wave Hotel Pattaya — an 18-Room Art Deco Boutique on the Beachfront
intro: Among the towering hotels lining Central Pattaya Beach sits a low pastel building with the soft curves of Art Deco, tucked right across from the sea — Wave Hotel Pattaya, a tiny 18-room boutique that brings 1940s Miami Beach to the heart of town · Run by Sukosol Hotels, every room has a private balcony facing Pattaya Bay and measures around 45 sqm · There's a beachfront pool and the Cadillac Café & Bar on the ground floor · You can cross to the sand and walk to CentralFestival in minutes · From approx ฿2,800/night · Score 9.5 from 92 Trip.com reviews.
galleryAlts: An Art Deco styled room at Wave Hotel Pattaya in warm tones with a sea-view balcony
The beachfront swimming pool at Wave Hotel Pattaya looking out over Pattaya Bay
Cadillac Café & Bar on the ground floor of Wave Hotel, styled like 1940s Miami

body.html: Wave Hotel is a boutique property by Sukosol Hotels, sitting right on Central Pattaya's Beach Road directly across from the sea — and what sets it apart from a typical Pattaya hotel is its Art Deco design, inspired by 1940s Miami Beach · It's a low, curved building in pastel tones, with the lines and neon glow of South Beach · At just 18 rooms, many guests say it feels more like staying in a design home than a chain hotel.

All 18 rooms run from around 45 sqm and up — noticeably larger than the standard rooms of similar-tier hotels in this area · They're done in warm Art Deco tones with comfy beds, flatscreen TVs, a fridge and the in-room tech you'd want · Every room has a private balcony facing Pattaya Bay · The honest note from real reviews is that the balconies are fairly small with little shade, and a few bathrooms have compact shower space — but cleanliness and bed comfort pass with flying colours in almost every review.
"Small hotel but seriously stylish — open the balcony door and the whole of Pattaya Bay is right there. The staff remembered our names after just two nights; we felt like VIPs."

The thing guests rave about most is the service · Being a small hotel, the staff look after you closely — many reviews call them the warmest, most attentive team they've met in Thailand · They remember names and handle the little things before you even ask · Breakfast is à la carte, cooked to order rather than a buffet, which most people love because it arrives hot and fresh — though a few note the menu has fewer choices than a big hotel.

The ground floor is home to the Cadillac Café & Bar, styled with the glamour of 1940s Miami and offering both indoor and outdoor seating · The pool is a small beachfront one with a Cabana Bar — not a giant infinity pool, but a quiet, private corner looking out over Pattaya Bay · Guests here to genuinely relax love the calm of it; anyone expecting a big pool or full resort facilities should adjust expectations, because this is a small boutique hotel.

Location is the big advantage · It's right on Central Pattaya's Beach Road — cross the street to the sand, walk to CentralFestival in about 2–3 minutes, and reach Walking Street in roughly 15 · There are hundreds of restaurants within walking distance · The trade-off, shared by every Beach Road hotel, is noise from the beachfront road and nightlife after dark · Rooms facing the street can catch some — light sleepers should ask for a higher floor and keep the balcony door closed at night.

Honestly, Wave Hotel suits people who want a stylish design hotel with close personal service in a central beachfront spot more than those chasing a private-beach resort or a big pool · Rates start around ฿2,800/night on a low-season weekday, rising to ฿4,000–4,700+ at weekends and in high season (the official rate usually includes breakfast for two) · With 9.5 on Trip.com and 4.8/5 from 463 TripAdvisor reviews (ranked #32 of 619 hotels in Pattaya), this is a little boutique that guests genuinely love — and a fitting pick for couples or anyone wanting a hotel with real character in the middle of Central Pattaya Beach.

honestSummary: Wave Hotel is a small boutique that suits people wanting a hotel with real character and close personal service in a central beachfront spot — gorgeous Art Deco, every room sea-facing, walk to the mall and beach · Just know it's an 18-room hotel: the pool is small and facilities aren't full-resort, and the area has noise at night.
honestChecks: If you want a private-beach resort with a big pool and full facilities — this is an 18-room boutique with a small pool, not a full resort → look at InterContinental or Centara Grand Mirage instead
If you're a light sleeper sensitive to noise — Beach Road brings traffic and nightlife sound at night → ask for a higher, inner-facing room and keep the balcony door shut at night
If you're going on a weekend or in high season — with only 18 rooms it fills fast and rates climb → book ahead and lock a free-cancellation rate early

tips.title: Ask for a Sunset room for the full sea view
tips.body: Twilight rooms face the side/city; Sunset and Ocean View face Pattaya Bay. Ask for a sea-facing room to get the most from the setting.

tips.title: Breakfast is à la carte
tips.body: It's not a buffet — everything's cooked to order from the menu, so it arrives hot. Try the egg dishes and freshly brewed coffee in the morning.

tips.title: Ask for a higher floor if noise bothers you
tips.body: Beach Road has nightlife sound at night. A higher floor with the balcony door closed makes for a far better night's sleep.

tips.title: Book ahead — a small hotel fills fast
tips.body: There are only 18 rooms; weekends and high season sell out quickly. Lock a free-cancellation rate first and confirm later.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Wave Hotel Pattaya

faq.q: Where is Wave Hotel Pattaya and what's nearby?
faq.a: Wave Hotel is at 310/3 Beach Road in Central Pattaya, directly across from the sea · Cross the street to the sand, walk to CentralFestival in about 2–3 minutes and Walking Street in roughly 15 · It's about 10 minutes' drive from Terminal 21 and around 40 minutes from U-Tapao Airport (UTP).

faq.q: How much does Wave Hotel Pattaya cost and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Rates start around ฿2,800/night for a Twilight Room on a low-season weekday · They rise to ฿4,000–4,700+ at weekends and in high season (the official rate usually includes breakfast for two) · Options run from Twilight, Sunset (sea view) and Ocean View Suite to a Family Room · Always compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: How many rooms does Wave Hotel Pattaya have and what's the design?
faq.a: It's a small boutique with 18 rooms in an Art Deco style inspired by 1940s Miami Beach · A low, curved pastel building, with every room around 45 sqm and a balcony facing Pattaya Bay · Run by Sukosol Hotels, with a focus on close, small-hotel service.

faq.q: Who is Wave Hotel Pattaya best for?
faq.a: It's best for couples and anyone wanting a hotel with real character and close personal service in a central beachfront spot · If you're after a private-beach resort with a big pool and full facilities, look at InterContinental or Centara Grand Mirage instead.

faq.q: Is Wave Hotel Pattaya noisy from the nightlife?
faq.a: Because it's on Beach Road, there is some traffic and nightlife sound at night · Street-facing rooms catch it more clearly · If you're worried about noise, ask for a higher floor and keep the balcony door closed at night for a much better sleep.

faq.q: What's breakfast like at Wave Hotel Pattaya?
faq.a: Breakfast is à la carte, cooked fresh to order rather than a buffet · The upside is it arrives hot and freshly made, which most guests prefer · It's served at the Cadillac Café & Bar on the ground floor · Some packages include breakfast for two — always check when you book.
